drag_model.formula: Cd = base_cd + fin_cd_per_area_ratio * (total fin planform area / body cross-section area) + marginal_wobble_cd (only if static margin is marginal)
drag_model.source: MADE UP coefficients. The fin term is roughly skin friction on both faces (2 x Cf of about 0.004) plus thickness and interference drag. The wobble penalty is a gameplay number for the Sim Spec v2 section 2.5 rule.

nose_mass_model.formula: nose mass (when not given) = pi * R * slant_length * material areal_density_kg_m2 * areal_factor
nose_mass_model.source: MADE UP. A nose fairing is a thin unpressurised shell with no bulkheads or plumbing, so it weighs far less per square metre than the all-up tank-wall figure in materials.json. 0.35 makes a 3 m wide, 6 m long fairing about 470 kg.

nose_shapes.name: Cone
nose_shapes.source: X factor and CN_alpha: Barrowman, 'Calculating the Center of Pressure of a Model Rocket' (Centuri TIR-33), as quoted in Sim Spec v2 section 2.1. base_cd and cg_fraction are MADE UP ballparks.

nose_shapes.name: Ogive
nose_shapes.description: The classic curved rocket nose. Lowest drag.
nose_shapes.source: X factor and CN_alpha: Barrowman (Centuri TIR-33), as quoted in Sim Spec v2 section 2.1. base_cd and cg_fraction are MADE UP ballparks.

nose_shapes.name: Parabolic
nose_shapes.description: A rounded tip that blends smoothly into the body.
nose_shapes.source: X factor and CN_alpha: Barrowman (Centuri TIR-33), as quoted in Sim Spec v2 section 2.1. base_cd and cg_fraction are MADE UP ballparks.

nose_shapes.name: Blunt capsule
nose_shapes.description: Short and fat, like a capsule. Lots of drag, but roomy.
nose_shapes.source: X factor is Barrowman's value for an ELLIPSOID nose (0.333 L), used here as a stand-in for a blunt capsule: the Sim Spec gives no blunt factor. base_cd and cg_fraction are MADE UP ballparks.
